title: Adaptive spectral phase scheduler for initgen+decode with tenant-aware fairness and kernel hints
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Prefill/initgen and decode phase splitting is a critical lever for balancing tail latency vs throughput. Current heuristics use fixed token-count thresholds and coarse tenant weights which leads to either unnecessary phase overhead (too many micro-phases) or long tails for latency-sensitive tenants. Kernel selection and attention-cost variability across prompts further complicate scheduling.

Proposal: Implement an Adaptive Spectral Phase Scheduler (ASPS) that uses lightweight spectral estimates of attention cost and runtime kernel latency profiles to decide split points, admission, and hedging policies per-request and per-tenant. ASPS combines three components: (1) Offline kernel/attention profiling to build per-model spectral cost curves and kernel latency models; (2) Runtime spectral estimator that samples early attention/length signals and maps to predicted cost buckets; (3) A tenant-aware policy layer that trades off latency SLOs vs throughput/efficiency using soft quotas and fast demotion to lower-cost kernels when capacity constrained.

Key design points:
- Spectral estimator: scalar signatures computed from prompt length, attention sparsity proxy (e.g., estimated non-zero density from tokenizer heuristics), and initial KV cache hit patterns. Must be <200us to avoid adding latency.
- Kernel hinting: estimator emits a kernel preference score (fast-quantized vs high-accuracy) and expected per-token ms. Scheduler uses this during admission and while deciding to split a phase.
- Phase splitting: rather than fixed token windows, ASPS computes a marginal-latency-per-token curve and picks split points where incremental cost crosses tenant latency headroom threshold. This allows occasional longer micro-batches when kernel is cheap and shorter splits when attention cost spikes.
- Fairness: tenants register SLO class (low-latency, best-effort) and a weight. ASPS enforces fairness via a soft-token budget that decays over time and priority bumping for tenants that have suffered tail violations.
- Hedging & fallback: for requests predicted to exceed latency budget, scheduler can trigger speculative parallel decode on a demoted kernel (lower-accuracy quant) and cancel slower path on early completion.
- Observability: emit per-request predicted cost bucket, chosen split points, kernel hint, and actual latency/cost. Add rollout dashboard with percentiles by tenant and model.

Success criteria (metrics):
- 99th percentile latency for low-latency tenants down by >=15% on mixed workloads compared to baseline scheduler.
- Overall token throughput unchanged or within -5% with latency SLO improvements.
- Kernel fallback rate <5% in steady state.

Risks & mitigations:
- Estimator misprediction: mitigate with conservative hedging, and warm-up period using conservative defaults.
- Oscillation between kernels causing cache churn: add dampening window during which kernel choice is sticky for a request and neighboring microbatches when possible.
- Fairness starvation under extreme load: implement hard cap per-tenant emergency reserve and circuit breaker.

Rollout plan:
1) Offline profiling job to generate spectral cost curves for top 10 models (runtime-1.21).
2) Local simulator integration (existing scheduling sim) to validate policy across recorded traces.
3) Canary in a small dedicated pool with synthetic latency-sensitive tenants.
4) Monitor metrics and expand to 10% of production traffic before full rollout.

Artifacts & links: PRD: https://confluence.internal/redwood/asps-prd (draft), Simulation notebook: drive://redwood/sim/asps-sim.ipynb, Related tickets: ENG-271828 (congestion controller), ENG-51234 (granular splitter).
